_note: First-visit tips, shown once per screen. Placeholders in {braces} are filled from data/level1.json so the text never goes stale: {goal}, {mass_kg}, {budget}, {deadline}, {weeks}, {goal_mb}, {reserve_pct}.

briefing.title: Briefing
steps: You must stay inside the limits: at most {mass_kg} kg, a budget of {budget}, and launch by day {deadline}.
The grey locked choices (bigger craft, higher orbit) are not available in this level. Click one to see why.

workshop.title: Workshop
steps: Build your satellite here. Click a part in the tray at the bottom, or drag it onto the satellite, to fit it. Slots that are still empty and required show in yellow.
The six bars on the right check your design. Green is fine, yellow is close to the limit, red means a check fails. Hover a bar, or press Why red?, to see what is wrong.
Time is money. Every day of building costs staff pay and pushes launch later, and the deadline is day {deadline}. Press Pause to stop the clock while you think.
Stay under {mass_kg} kg and {budget}. When you are ready, press Test it.

test_lab.title: Test lab
steps: The test lab checks your design against every requirement. PASS means it is fine, FAIL means it is not.
Each red card tells you why a check failed and gives a tip. Fix it sends you back to the workshop, and a failed test costs time.
You may Launch anyway with failed checks, but each one has a consequence once the satellite is in orbit.

ops.title: Operations
steps: Your satellite flies for {weeks} weeks. One week passes every few seconds. The goal is {goal_mb} MB of photos delivered to the ground.
You can switch on Safe mode (no photos, the battery recovers), Smaller photos (less data, so storage fills slower) or buy an extra ground pass (costs money, then needs time to recharge).
Events will pop up and ask you to choose. What you built earlier can change how an event turns out.

report.title: Report
steps: You can earn up to three stars: one for reaching the goal, one for passing every check, and one for finishing with {reserve_pct}% of the budget left.
Why it happened explains, step by step, what went wrong. Retry with changes keeps your parts so you can fix just the problem.
